title: How MotoGP Bikes Lean So Far Without Falling

voice.pace: controlled, visual-first, with clean pauses at each physics reveal

segments.text: At extreme lean, a MotoGP bike looks ready to fall. So why doesn't it?
segments.visual_cue: Front-view motorcycle freezes at lean with an illustrative angle arc.

segments.text: Gravity pulls down, while the road pushes up and inward. Lean aligns the combined bike and rider with that road force.
segments.visual_cue: Gravity, lateral grip, and resultant road-force vectors appear.

segments.text: This small contact patch supplies the lateral force that bends the path. Body position never removes that demand.
segments.visual_cue: Tyre contact patch and lateral shear arrows fill the frame.

segments.text: For the same speed and radius, hanging off shifts the combined center of mass inward. The same required combined lean can use less motorcycle lean.
segments.visual_cue: Aligned and hanging-off riders share the same illustrative combined lean.

segments.text: That can create tyre and chassis clearance, or useful operating margin. On exit, the rider recenters as the bike stands up.
segments.visual_cue: Motorcycle and rider smoothly return toward upright while the center of mass remains highlighted.

segments.text: The goal is not maximum lean. It is the right combined geometry. Lean smarter, not just further.
segments.visual_cue: Final headline: LEAN SMARTER. NOT JUST FURTHER.
